entities.summary: Beorhtric was the King of Wessex from 786 to 802 CE, succeeding Cynewulf. His reign was marked by the reign of his wife, Cynehild, and her father-in-law, Cynewulf's brother, Ealdwulf. During this period, the Kingdom of Wessex expanded its territories through several military campaigns, including the Battle of Hoxne, where Beorhtric defeated the Viking invaders. Beorhtric's legacy is significant in the context of Anglo-Saxon history, as he played a crucial role in shaping the political and military landscape of Wessex. His reign also saw the development of the kingdom's administrative and economic systems, including the establishment of a powerful and centralized government. The influence of Beorhtric can be seen in the subsequent reigns of his successors, who continued to expand Wessex's territories and consolidate its power. Beorhtric's life and reign serve as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, which continue to shape our understanding of medieval European history. The Beowulf poem, which tells the story of a hero named Beowulf, who fights against the forces of Grendel and the dragon, is often linked to Beorhtric's reign, although this connection is subject to debate among historians. In any case, Beorhtric's name has become synonymous with the golden age of Wessex, a period of relative peace and prosperity that followed the tumultuous Viking raids of the 9th century. Beorhtric's death in 802 CE marked the end of an era, but his legacy lived on through his successors, who continued to build on the foundations laid by the great King Beorhtric.
